# PropertyField

The frame every property of a Pointr Cloud item sits in (CLOUD-UI-004): a bordered group with the property's name as its caption, an info button that says what the property is, and a red trash button that removes it. A Dashboard module: it ships from `@kozmos-ds/react/dashboard`, with `@kozmos-ds/react/dashboard.css` loaded after the package's `style.css`, and only on the web.

- **Import:** `import { PropertyField } from "@kozmos-ds/react/dashboard";`
- **Stylesheet:** `import "@kozmos-ds/react/dashboard.css";`, after the package's `style.css`: a Dashboard module's rules are in this sheet alone.
- **Group:** Dashboard
- **Platforms:** React; not linked to Figma yet.
- **Storybook:** <https://vodoco.github.io/kozmos-design-system/storybook/?path=/docs/dashboard-propertyfield--docs>

## Example

From its `Default` story.

```tsx
import {
  MultiSelect,
  NumberInput,
  Select,
  SelectContent,
  SelectItem,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
  Stack,
  ThemeProvider,
} from "@kozmos-ds/react";
import { PropertyField } from "@kozmos-ds/react/dashboard";

const occupancy = [
  { value: "available", label: "Available" },
  { value: "occupied", label: "Occupied" },
  { value: "underConstruction", label: "Under construction" },
  { value: "temporarilyClosed", label: "Temporarily closed" },
];

const restrictions = [
  { value: "invite-only", label: "Invite only" },
  { value: "membership-required", label: "Membership required" },
  { value: "booking-required", label: "Booking required" },
  { value: "ticket-required", label: "Ticket required" },
];

export function PropertyFieldExample() {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider defaultTheme="light">
      <Stack gap={3}>
        <PropertyField
          name="Capacity"
          info="How many people the space holds at once."
          onRemove={() => {}}
        >
          <NumberInput aria-label="Capacity" defaultValue={120} min={0} />
        </PropertyField>
        <PropertyField name="Occupancy Status" onRemove={() => {}}>
          <Select defaultValue="underConstruction">
            <SelectTrigger aria-label="Occupancy Status">
              <SelectValue />
            </SelectTrigger>
            <SelectContent>
              {occupancy.map((option) => (
                <SelectItem key={option.value} value={option.value}>
                  {option.label}
                </SelectItem>
              ))}
            </SelectContent>
          </Select>
        </PropertyField>
        <PropertyField name="Access Restrictions" onRemove={() => {}}>
          <MultiSelect
            aria-label="Access Restrictions"
            options={restrictions}
            defaultValue={["invite-only", "booking-required"]}
          />
        </PropertyField>
      </Stack>
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

## PropertyField

The frame every property added to a Pointr Cloud item sits in
(CLOUD-UI-004): a bordered group with the property's name as its caption,
an info button for what the property is, and a red trash button that
removes it. The group is named by its caption, and both buttons have a
name, `About <name>` and `Remove <name>` (Cloud's had none).

A Dashboard module (decision 183): import it from
`@kozmos-ds/react/dashboard`, with `@kozmos-ds/react/dashboard.css` after
the package's style.css.

It forwards its ref to `HTMLDivElement`. Its props are `PropertyFieldProps`, which extends `Omit<React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "children">`.

- `name`: `string`, **required**.

  The property's name: the group's caption, and its accessible name.

- `info`: `React.ReactNode`, optional.

  What the property is, opened from the info button beside the caption
  (a click, Enter or Space, as a toggletip: a tooltip cannot be reached by
  touch). Unset, no info button.

- `infoLabel`: `string`, optional.

  The info button's name. Default `About <name>`.

- `onRemove`: `() => void`, optional.

  Removes the property from the item. Drawn as the red trash button
  beside the group, Kozmos's destructive tone (`emotion="danger"`).
  Unset, no button.

- `removeLabel`: `string`, optional.

  The remove button's name. Default `Remove <name>`.

- `children`: `React.ReactNode`, optional.

  The property's editor: a field, or one of the Dashboard editors.

It also takes the attributes React's DOM types give it (`className`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, the event handlers among them).
